claims.text: Optimized annealing followed by rapid quenching will refine the grain structure of MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials.
The proposed treatment will produce a controlled or optimal dislocation density.
The resulting microstructure will increase ductility and toughness.
The resulting microstructure will improve resistance to fatigue.
The treatment will retain the sharp magneto-structural transition and a large magnetocaloric effect.
Pristine MnNiSi-based intermetallic materials have coarse grains.
Pristine MnNiSi-based intermetallic materials are highly brittle and have poor mechanical performance.
Pristine MnNiSi-based materials possess a well-defined magneto-structural transition that yields a large magnetic entropy change.
The annealing temperature should be near the magneto-structural transition and should be followed by rapid quenching.
The treatment should be performed under magnetic fields typical of refrigeration cooling cycles.
Grain refinement can enhance tensile strength while retaining ductility.
Fine grains and a controlled dislocation network distribute stress more evenly.
Fine grains and a controlled dislocation network arrest or inhibit crack propagation.
Avoiding compositional dilution and detrimental secondary phases will preserve the abrupt magneto-structural transition.
Treated samples will have greater tensile strength, ductility, fracture toughness, and fatigue resistance than untreated samples.
The magnetic entropy change of treated samples will remain within approximately 10–15% of the untreated baseline.
Excessive grain growth or unwanted phase transformations may compromise mechanical performance.
Excessive grain growth or unwanted phase transformations may compromise magnetocaloric performance.
